claims.text: The baseline [TaNb]0.31(TiZrHf)0.69 alloy has a body-centered-cubic structure.
The baseline alloy is fully chemically disordered.
Average valence electron count is the dominant parameter governing superconducting transition temperature in single-phase high-entropy superconductors.
Changing average valence electron count while retaining the disordered bcc lattice will produce predictable changes in Tc.
Changing average valence electron count while retaining the disordered bcc lattice will produce predictable changes in Hc2.
Substitution between constituents with different valence electron counts can vary average VEC while approximately preserving atomic size and crystal structure.
Homogeneous elemental distribution in the disordered lattice mediates changes in the density of states at the Fermi level.
Average VEC determines the density of states near the Fermi level.
The density of states near the Fermi level dictates electron-phonon coupling strength.
Phonon-mediated superconductivity occurs in the closely related uranium-containing alloy [TaNb]0.31(TiUHf)0.69.
Increasing VEC toward an optimal range enhances electron-phonon coupling and raises Tc.
Increasing VEC toward an optimal range raises Hc2.
Reducing VEC while holding structure and disorder constant lowers Tc relative to the baseline.
Elements such as uranium can exert pair-breaking effects and suppress superconductivity.
The predicted VEC trend applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase disordered solid solution with at least five elements present at no less than 5 at.% each.
Local disorder, lattice distortion, magnetic effects, and disorder-induced phonon-spectrum changes may also affect Tc.
Absence of a systematic directional relationship between VEC and Tc under constant phase and disorder would falsify VEC dominance.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires changing constituent concentrations through substitution, whereas the conditions say to maintain the total concentration of each element. Taken literally, both requirements cannot be met; the intended condition may instead be that every retained element remains at or above 5 at.%.
